newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ZEPHIR CONSORTIUM SLAMS ROMANIA GSM TENDER RESULT.
newsitem.headline: ZEPHIR CONSORTIUM SLAMS ROMANIA GSM TENDER RESULT.

text.p: A consortium led by telecom groups Motorola Inc of the U.S. and Tele Danmark of Denmark said on Wednesday it contested the results of a tender to install and operate a GSM system in Romania.

In a statement, the Zephir consortium asked Romania's Communications Ministry to appoint a "neutral consulting agency" to reconsider the evaluation procedures of the offers submitted by the six consortia which took part in the bid.

Last week, the ministry said consortia led by AirTouch Communications Inc of the U.S. and France Telecom had won the two licences offered in the bid to install and operate a digital GSM system in the Balkan country.
Norway's Telenor, Romania's private Radiotel Group and Rokura communications operators are also part of Zephir.

Zephir said the commission which had evaluated the offers -- the Monaco-based La Compagnie de Conseil, part of La Compagnie Financiere Edmond de Rothschild (CFER) of France -- has "compromised the objectivity of a neutral consultant".
Ministry officials were not available for comment. A source said the ministry was expected to answer Zephir's claims on Friday, when the deadline to submit objections expires.

The other four consortia which competed in the tender included Telefonica Romania, a joint venture between Telefonica de Espana and Romania's state telecoms network, and Italy's telecoms group Stet Spa .

Zephir's protests on Wednesday added to threats last week by Telefonica to take legal steps against the outcome of the tender on grounds it "violates the rights conceded (by the ministry) in March 1992 to Telefonica Romania."
Telefonica said its Romanian branch had been promised the right over digital mobile telephone service when it started an analogue service in Bucharest in 1992.
The ministry rejected the accusations as groundless.
The tender requires the companies to cover within the next 18 months of winning the tender the main cities, as well as to provide GSM coverage along European transit routes in Romania.
A licence has a ten-year validity and a frequency concession tax amounts to $50 million per licence. Estimated value of the project is $1.0 billion. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
